english.title: Contravene Part 2 Notice - general provisions
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being subject to a notice issued under Part 2 of the National Security Act 2023, without reasonable excuse, contravened a measure specified in that notice in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 56(1) and (4) of the National Security Act 2023.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being subject to a notice issued under Part 2 of the National Security Act 2023
without reasonable excuse
contravened a measure specified in that notice

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Schedule 7 details the measures that may be imposed under a Part 2 notice. This offence should not be used in relation to contravention of a a Part 2 notice containing a travel measure, which carries a higher penalty and is subject to a separate offence document, see H101460.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or fine.
Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
